chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Losing a gig to Al Morgan, and why he never took a steady job
summary: A gig for C.C. Caldwell goes to Al Morgan; Callender says it spurred him to show them, and that the Armstrong stint taught him the advantage of reading music.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Around that same time, Cab Calloway's band was out here, and Al Morgan went with the... Al Morgan had quit Cab's band. And I remember being hired for a gig out in Gardenia, at a place called Gloria Nightclub. C.C. Caldwell had the band. And I was hired for this gig, so I go out to the gig, and I get to the door, and I hear a bass in there tuning up. I wonder what's happening. So I go to the door with my little bass, and Al Morgan is on the stand, and they say to me, "Sorry, kid, we got Al Morgan."
Well, you know, those kinds of things hurt, but it didn't hurt so much that it didn't give me more determination than ever to show them. And years later, I did show them.
Well, I managed to become a fairly decent bass player and tuba player, and work in the studios..
Oh, yeah. I thought maybe you meant some specific incident with them.

No, not with them. But those things hurt, and at the time they happen you say, 'I'll show them.' So I did. But it didn't feel so good when I showed them, you know I just went on to be a better musician than I'd probably have been if they had hired me. Because those guys believed in staying on the job year-in and year-out, and I knew you couldn't learn anything like that. So consequently, I can't ever consider myself as having had a steady job. I figured the more I know about music, the more I'll be able to work. So having a steady job has never worried me. I've always been able to work.
At that very young age, was that brief time with Louis Armstrong a learning experience for you?

Well, you see, at that time people were surprised when bass players or drummers could read music. But I had learned to read before I ever could play an instrument, so that was one advantage. Well, yeah, that gave me...
